  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION

Tuesday, February 15, 2022  7:00 PM  City Council Chambers

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a Special Meeting of the Park & Activities Commission of the City of
Rolling Hills Estates will be held on Tuesday, February 15, 2022 at 7:00 p.m. via Video Teleconference. The
agenda for the special meeting with the items to be discussed is set forth below.

Public Participation Information
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493
  and proposed Resolution No. 2498, due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and
  social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held
  remotely via teleconference. There will not be a physical location for this meeting. Members of the public
  may participate in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 841 3588 4893 Meeting Password: 355733. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 841 3588 4893, Meeting Password: 355733. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION SPECIAL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 15, 2022

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A Special meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 7:04 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s Executive
  Order N-29-20.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope,
  Retz, Romanelli

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Daniel A-Haja

  4.  PRESENTATION

  A.  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the City Council appointed
  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA as Chair and COMMISSIONER BAIN as Vice Chair
  of the COMMISSION.

  COMMISSIONER POPE was recognized for her service as 2021 Chair of the
  Commission and was provided a plaque for her service.

  5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES  COMMISSION  MEETING  DRAFT  MINUTES  OF
  DECEMBER 13, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  B.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF JANUARY
  18, 2022

  COMMISSIONER POPE noted a question on page 6 that was attributed to her but
  it may have been posed by COMMISSIONER BAIN.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
FEBRUARY 15, 2022
   VICE CHAIR BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to:

  APPROVE MINUTES AS REVISED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  NEW PROGRAM PROPOSAL – SPORTBALL

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the staff
  report.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if rugby would be offered. Community Services
  Supervisor Pinuelas responded that rugby would be offered as an alternative to golf
  as golf balls are not allowed in the park.

  Amanda Richie of Sportball added that rugby would be only for one week and would
  look into piloting a tot-style rugby program for the summer.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked about Sportball’s experience with other cities.
  Amanda Richie responded that the franchise is experienced with Los Angeles and
  Orange County cities. She added that classes range from 8 to 15 students per
  instructor and that the pandemic affected classes, but most are waitlisted. She also
  stated cities like Manhattan Beach have received the program well.
  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked about the franchise. Amanda Richie noted the
  program is a 25-year-old franchise which operates in the United States, Canada,
  and Singapore and that she is the owner of the South Bay and Orange County
  territories. She also stated the program was developed using pediatric clinical
  research behind the style and format of the programs.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about park utilization and the bowl area at
  Ernie Howlett Park and the soccer field of AYSO at Highridge. He asked if there
  would be any overlap or conflict in scheduling. Community Services Coordinator
  A-Haja noted that there is plenty of room to accommodate both classes and parties
  as has been done in the past with other youth sports groups.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if Amanda Richie has walked the parks.
  Amanda Richie responded that she has visited Ernie Howlett Park but not Highridge
  and will assess it later. He asked how large the Sportball staff was. Amanda Richie
  noted having 16 coaches including her and her husband.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 15, 2022
   COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked about the maximum number of students
  per class. Amanda Richie noted the maximum number of students is 15 per coach
  but could be increased with more coaches. Younger students aged five and below
  have parents included in the class. She noted classes do take some time to
  increase and noted the weekend classes are prime time for most families.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked about parking for classes and noted issues
  with Highridge parking and asked about fees and how they compare to other cities.
  Amanda Richie noted some variables which factor into the fees such as household
  income of the area, contract splits, whether they are city contractors, and resident
  and non-resident pricing. He asked staff if references have been verified.
  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded that if approved, municipal
  references would be contacted, and Amanda Richie noted customer references are
  available on their social media.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the difficulty in parking at Highridge and that
  dropping off kids to those classes may be too far and asked if the classes were
  additive or in lieu of one of the classes. Amanda Richie responded that both have
  been done in the past but have done drop-off style classes. Summer weekday
  classes are typically drop-off but could also have parents in attendance if desired.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if the classes taking place on the weekend
  would interfere with picnics and how the public would be notified. Community
  Services Coordinator A-Haja responded that staff would let prospective park
  permits know of the class schedule so that spaces won’t overlap. He added that
  classes take up a small footprint and should accommodate most permits.
  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas added that Highridge is just a secondary
  option, and that Ernie Howlett Park would be the primary location for these classes.

  COMMISSIONER POPE wanted to ensure that space would be available during
  summer turf renovation and the gopher abatement. ACM Davis responded it would
  be similar to past programs, such as TGA, and a gopher maintenance program is
  currently being used.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked staff if the grass bowl usage would conflict
  with park permits. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja responded that staff
  typically splits up the grass bowl area into different quadrants which could
  accommodate permits and classes and noted other grass areas where classes
  could be held.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted one way to avoid conflict would be to ensure
  tennis staff know the class schedules of the classes at the park and their locations
  so that patrons could avoid those areas.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 15, 2022
   COMMISSIONER BAIN asked what type of training the coaches have. Amanda
  Richie provided an overview of her staff training.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if the coaches have CPR training. Amanda
  Richie affirmed and added that they carry first aid equipment with them and are Live
  Scanned and background checked.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked what obligations the City would have in promoting
  the program and how Sportball sponsors their programs. Amanda Richie
  responded that the program is open to cross promotion on different platforms.
  Marketing will also will include the City Community Services department newsletter,
  City website, social media posts. She added that their email marketing list includes
  people who follow their page that their past students can register for upcoming
  programs, that they use tags to reach specific demographics, and community
  events can be used to promote the program. Community Services Supervisor
  Pinuelas also added that the program would be contracted under the same
  guidelines as other City recreation contractors.

  COMMISSIONER POPE moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA as
  follows:

  ACCEPT STAFF RECOMMENDATION AND APPROVE THE ADDITION
  OF SPORTBALL SOUTH BAY PROGRAM AS A CITY RECREATION
  CLASS.

  AYES:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Retz, Romanelli
  ABSENT:  None

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  B.  PICKLEBALL COURTS

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja provided a brief overview of the staff
  report.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked about the demand for pickleball courts when
  comparing the number of courts from six to eight. ACM Davis noted increasing
  demand for the sport and demand from players locally but noted expansion could
  be possible in the future. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja noted 70% of
  survey takers are in favor of pickleball at the tennis courts and that 50% of pickleball
  and tennis players are interested in sharing courts.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN added that she attempted pickleball play herself and noted
  the popularity of the sport especially at the South Bay Tennis Center. She shared
  that the pickleball coach noted the busy class schedule and the facility’s open play

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
FEBRUARY 15, 2022
   for it. She shared that she took a private class from a private instructor and noted
  the coach was also an ambassador for the sport and could help in future pickleball
  play at Ernie Howlett. She liked the idea of the six courts but would not be surprised
  if eight courts would be needed once the word gets out, as demand is growing for
  the sport. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja agreed and added the desire
  from the South Bay Tennis Center’s pickleball coach to teach at Ernie Howlett.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI shared that he spoke to the Ernie Howlett Tennis
  Pro and noted their lukewarm reception of the pickleball courts and said they
  preferred four pickleball courts split between tennis courts 5 and 6. He stated that
  he would like to proceed but shared that adding four pickleball courts may be too
  much due to heavy tennis utilization. He stated that the Tennis Pro preferred baby
  steps. He also stated the added expense of $10,000 for fencing to get four pickleball
  courts on tennis courts 5 and 6 should consider the period of return on that
  investment. After listening to the Tennis Pro, he can support four court overlays on
  two tennis courts after knowing with growth provision to add two more pickleball
  courts that would go on tennis court 7 with proof of support.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked how long it would take to restripe tennis court 7 to
  add two additional pickleball courts. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja
  responded about a week to allow for striping and curing.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if the cities on the hill have pickleball courts
  and if so, how many. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja responded the
  pickleball courts are not as many as south bay clubs but are increasing. ACM Davis
  noted the Palos Verdes Tennis Club did convert some tennis courts to pickleball
  courts with a waitlist and that the Peninsula Racquet Club has a pickleball program
  that shares with tennis courts. She added that most clubs on the hill have pickleball
  courts with some type of program. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK added
  Peninsula Racquet Club has eight pickleball courts and that they seem popular.
  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the Manhattan Beach private tennis club also
  converted some tennis courts to pickleball courts and that pickleball courts were
  added near the private residential area near Highridge. She added that she hoped
  that the City could adopt some courts as well. She noted the temporary pickleball
  lines were not favorable due to court set up times and that permanent lines would
  encourage more pickleball play.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked how the pickleball court usage could be
  tracked. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja responded that tennis office staff
  could track the number of hours the pickleball courts are used and tracked for future
  reports.

  CHAIR CIAROLLA asked if there would be a conflict in tennis court reservations
  with pickleball use. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja responded that the

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
FEBRUARY 15, 2022
   current hierarchy of reservations holds tennis pros at the top, followed by tennis
  leagues and finally school teams would not currently be affected.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if there was a cost difference when adding
  the two courts. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja noted the additional cost
  should be around the cost of the overlay as the court would already be resurfaced
  but could confirm with the vendor. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK agreed with
  starting with four pickleball courts and adding two more if demand is there.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked for clarification of the number of pickleball courts
  desired. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja clarified that four pickleball
  courts would be overlayed on two tennis courts. She wanted to know why there
  was hesitation in going for six pickleball courts initially over three tennis courts.
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted that the only way to truly know the desire for
  pickleball would be to start with an initial four courts and track usage for a year
  before adding the two pickleball courts to court 7.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK stated putting four pickleball courts on one tennis
  court could save a tennis court for use. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI responded
  that putting four pickleball courts on any court would incur additional fencing and
  masonry costs.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked for clarification of the tennis courts being discussed.
  Staff shared an aerial image of the tennis courts for clarification. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI pointed out the courts used as well as the 45-degree angles which
  would need to be squared off. COMMISSIONER BAIN asked for clarification
  regarding how the overlays would be positioned on the tennis courts Staff clarified
  the costs needed to accommodate the four pickleball courts on a tennis court.
  COMMISSIONER BAIN agreed with incremental progress in the addition of the
  pickleball court overlays.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if converting from two pickleball courts per tennis
  court to four pickleball courts would affect resurfacing in the future.
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted it would not be possible unless expanding
  the concrete and fencing. COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if that were the case,
  would the court need to be repainted. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja
  noted the expansion would be two pickleball courts on tennis court 7, rather than
  increasing the fencing and masonry work to fit four pickleball courts on a tennis
  court. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted having two pickleball courts per tennis
  court would save additional costs of expanding the fencing and masonry work and
  that overlays could be added to court 7 if there is desire to expand.
  COMMISSIONER BAIN added that if further desire for pickleball occurs, court 8
  could also be used for an additional two pickleball courts.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
FEBRUARY 15, 2022
   COMMISSIONER BAIN stated that she prefers six courts over the initially proposed
  four and that she does not see the tennis courts being used to capacity unless there
  is a tournament. ACM Davis noted that use tapers off in the afternoons.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted that the City would not be the first to adopt
  pickleball and should reach out to other clubs to gauge their own pickleball program
  capacity.

  COMMISSIONER POPE agrees to assessing the pickleball usage after six months
  rather than a year and would like to vote on the matter.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if the paint would still be able to be overlayed after
  a year of use without additional cost. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja
  noted paint typically lasts five to six years and that he believed one year of use
  would be under warranty but that it could be confirmed by staff. COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK noted the changes proposed by COMMISSIONER RETZ would be
  longer term and could be done closer to the next resurfacing period to include fence
  and masonry expansion.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN stated that she would like to have staff bring back a
  proposal to manage the pickleball activity and future classes and that she is not
  sure the current tennis office staffing level could meet the possible increased
  demand for pickleball. ACM Davis asked if staff would be able to continue with the
  resurfacing project and bring back pickleball overlays as a separate item or if staff
  should concurrently overlay pickleball courts during resurfacing.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK stated that he was ok with four pickleball courts
  as an initial start. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI agreed and noted the pickleball
  courts would be needed to be able to study their usage.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI moved, seconded by CHAIR CIAROLLA as
  follows:

  ACCEPT STAFF RECOMMENDATION AND APPROVE THE ADDITION
  OF FOUR PICKLEBALL COURTS, TWO ON TENNIS COURT #5 AND
  TWO ON TENNIS COURT #6 CONCURRENT WITH THE COURT
  RESURFACING PROJECT AND COMPILE USAGE DATA FOR TWELVE
  MONTHS TO SEE IF GROWTH OF PICKLEBALL COURTS IS ENOUGH
  TO WARRANT ADDITIONAL OVERLAYS.

  AYES:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Retz, Romanelli
  ABSENT:  None

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
FEBRUARY 15, 2022
   C.  TENNIS COURT RENOVATION

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja provided a brief overview of the staff
  report.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked for clarification of the contract with Trueline
  and noted an error in the quote. Coordinator A-Haja stated that staff will clarify the
  amount and provide a revised corrected quote to the City Council.
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if the quote could be approved with a
  revision. ACM Davis noted it could be approved for the cost presented.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK as
  follows:

  APPROVE THE $57,022.40 BID WITH ADMONISHMENT TO VERIFY THE
  COST OF THE PICKLEBALL COURTS AND PROVIDE THAT ACCURATE
  PRICING TO COUNCIL FOR THE APPROVED CONTRACT.

  AYES:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Retz, Romanelli
  ABSENT:  None

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  D.  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECT LIST

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the staff
  report.

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided updates noting items such as a
  decrease in Eagle Scout projects and donations made by West Basin water drinking
  stations that have been installed. Highridge perimeter fencing will also be
  completed with additional openings to allow for better access once fencing post
  caps arrive within a week.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN commended staff for the Highridge fencing and noted that
  progress on the mural had slowed down at the park. She also noted the
  decomposed granite on the pathways showed some signs of being dug up.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded that it was due to ongoing
  grading due to past rains causing erosion and washouts. He added that gophers
  have been decreased by about 75% and turf renovations will commence again this
  year. COMMISSIONER BAIN also asked about the restroom flooring issue at Ernie
  Howlett. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith stated that wear and tear cause
  the porous concrete to be damaged and hold smells. Resurfacing and epoxy
  sealing the floors would keep the floors cleaner and hold less odors.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  8
FEBRUARY 15, 2022
   COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted the lookout point at George F Canyon could
  be looked at for adding a bench. He noted the moonlight walks could benefit from
  a gathering point. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted the storm in
  December 2021 destroyed a section of the area, additional work is needed such as
  fencing to make a pathway to the top.

  COMMISSIONER POPE likes the additional fence openings at Highridge Park and
  asked how long the turf renovations would take. Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith noted it occurs in late June and takes until late August but a later date
  helps seed germination. She asked if the rodent solution was applied to all parks.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith added City Hall to the list of parks, he also
  noted the method used to control the rodents were CO2 gas rather than traps which
  were more successful.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the difference in pricing for the EV
  stations. ACM Davis responded that the project is part of a Southern California
  Edison grant program that will pay for the infrastructure, the $79,000 is for the five
  stations themselves. The other program is part of the AQMD grant which only
  supports two charging stations with dual ports proposed for Ernie Howlett Park.
  COMMISSIONER BAIN commented that the Ernie Howlett Park cost was too high
  being a limited installation as the park could not support many stations there.
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that it may be due to the dirt parking lot
  limiting the installation process. ACM Davis noted Ernie Howlett Park grant is a
  matching grant in which AQMD matches $30,000 and the City pays for $30,000,
  details of the project are still being finalized. CHAIR CIAROLLA asked if the user
  pays the City for charging. ACM Davis responded that the user pays the City as
  they are considered City meters and that the City also sets the rate structure. She
  added that rates may be re-evaluated as more charging stations are added.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if a station could be installed in a dirt lot or if
  a concrete pad would be needed. ACM Davis responded it would be possible as
  long as it meets ADA requirements.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the importance of notifying the public that the
  charging stations are not free and that the City is paid in order to recoup costs.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  SNOW DAY (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated the event was rescheduled to
  Sunday February 27th due to Little League Opening Day on the 26th. The event will
  be from 10am to 12pm. Over 300 people were confirmed to attend via the
  Eventbrite website. Staff has contacted the snow vendor and due to the hilly nature
  of the grass bowl, there was no need for straw bales which enabled staff to

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  9
FEBRUARY 15, 2022
   purchase another three tons of snow. Up to 14 volunteers are expected to attend
  from local schools and the LA Donut food truck is also expected to attend to sell
  refreshments.
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if any sponsors were able to pick up the
  event. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded that a couple potential
  sponsors were reached out to but was open to any suggestions from the
  Commission.
  B.  MAYOR’S RIDE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)
  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted that May 7th was the projected date
  for the event and that the Boy Scouts were unable to attend this year. Staff plans
  on having the event catered again this year.

  9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted some wooden steps leading to the parking
  lot are loose. A drop off area near the trail could use fencing or signage on the
  steep drop nearby. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded that that
  area was also affected by the rain and that staff is working on the issue.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted the edge strip of the decomposed granite
  pathway to the drinking fountain is separated and sticking out in the air at Highridge
  Park, adding that it may need to be staked down. Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith responded that staff would remedy the issue the next day and that the
  last swing will be removed.

  COMMISSIONER POPE noted the sapling at Silver Spur Park is growing.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted losing past memorial trees and that
  gophers may have been eating their roots.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  None.

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JANUARY 25, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  10
FEBRUARY 15, 2022
